I should transcribe it as image markup or describe it. The instruction says "Text embedded in images (logos, stamps, accuracy-class markings, table scans, signatures) must be transcribed too." The eagle has no text. I could note it as an image. Maybe use a description like *[Bundesadler — German federal eagle emblem]*. But "do not annotate" — hmm. The rule says transcribe text embedded in images; the logo contains no text. I could include an image placeholder. To be safe, I'll include a bracketed description of the logo as image content. Actually the instructions say "Do not summarize, translate, annotate, or omit anything." A description isn't transcription of text. But the logo is an image element; best to include it as a markdown image alt text. I'll include `![Federal eagle emblem (Bundesadler)](...)` — but there's no URL. I'll just note it inline. I think the cleanest: transcribe the visible text; for the eagle, include something like *[Image: German federal eagle emblem]*. That's a reasonable interpretation of "transcribe images" when there's no text. The vertical "R3-0033" text on page 1 bottom left should be included. Now the table as HTML: ... but Minfill spans 4 columns with subheaders X(0.2), X(0.5), X(1), X(2).
